briefings.title: How To Build A Jet Engine From Scratch
briefings.tldr: After Rolls-Royce abruptly walked away from building the engine for Boom Supersonic’s 60-to-80-seat Overture airliner, Boom built its own engine core from scratch—and discovered it can first be deployed as a 42-megawatt natural-gas turbine for AI data centers, generating the cash flow and 1 million hours of operating data needed to fund and certify supersonic flight.

briefings.title: Bringing Supersonic Flight To The People
briefings.tldr: When Rolls-Royce abruptly walked away as Boom Supersonic's engine supplier, the startup took engine development in-house—ultimately unlocking "boomless" supersonic flight, creating a lucrative new 42-megawatt power turbine product line to power AI data centers, and enabling them to self-fund their passenger airliner without relying on external capital.

briefings.title: Blake Scholl: Why Plane Speed Stalled, Supersonic Commercial Flight, & Revolutionizing the Engine
briefings.tldr: Blake Scholl, founder and CEO of Boom Supersonic, discusses the company's milestones in developing supersonic commercial flight and pivoting its engine core technology to power high-demand data centers.
